outcome: Not settled as of 13 October 2026: no source found shows that the Liouville measure is the only quantum limit for negatively curved manifolds in general. Since 26 January 2024 the arithmetic and restricted cases moved (Hecke–Maass results in dimensions 2 to 4, a full unconditional QUE for one family of Pitale lifts on a non-compact quotient of H⁴ in March 2026, conditional and structural results), and no AI system is credited with any of it.
problem_asks: (1) A universal claim over every negatively curved Riemannian manifold M (the bullet's ‘negatively-curved manifold’; the literature takes M compact, since the normalised L²-mass needs finite volume; the bullet itself does not say compact, and no dimension is named, so every dimension of at least 2 is covered). (2) For each such M, along every sequence of Laplacian eigenfunctions φ_j with eigenvalues λ_j → ∞ (the whole sequence, not a density-one subsequence), the measures |φ_j|² dvol converge weak-* to the normalised Riemannian (Liouville) measure; equivalently, no subsequence concentrates on a closed geodesic or any other proper invariant set, and Liouville is the only semiclassical (quantum) limit. (3) The quantifier ‘large-frequency eigenfunctions’ is read in the Rudnick–Sarnak form as covering any orthonormal eigenbasis, not one distinguished basis such as a Hecke basis. Not asked: a rate, a particular eigenvalue set, or any support or entropy statement, which are routes to the claim rather than the claim itself.

events.what_happened: Elon Lindenstrauss, ‘Invariant measures and arithmetic quantum unique ergodicity’, Annals of Mathematics 163 (2006) 165–219. Proves arithmetic QUE for Hecke–Maass joint eigenfunctions on compact arithmetic hyperbolic surfaces, via measure rigidity for diagonal actions on Γ∖SL(2,R)×L. Pre-window; recorded as the base of the arithmetic line. The arXiv posting was not located.
events.revisions: Annals listing gives the title without ‘quantum’ (‘Invariant measures and arithmetic unique ergodicity’); no arXiv version located.
events.delivers: For compact arithmetic hyperbolic surfaces Γ∖H, weak-* convergence of |φ|² dvol to the uniform measure along any sequence of Hecke–Maass joint eigenfunctions with eigenvalue tending to infinity (per secondary sources, the paper also gives a weaker finite-volume statement). Restricted to arithmetic surfaces and to joint Hecke eigenfunctions.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks outside arithmetic Hecke eigenfunctions on compact arithmetic surfaces: general negatively curved manifolds, arbitrary orthonormal eigenbases, and dimensions above two.

checked_by.qualification: Expert survey author on the conjecture (Bulletin AMS 2011, ‘Recent progress on the quantum unique ergodicity conjecture’)
checked_by.what_they_did: Surveys the arithmetic result as the proven case; read at search-snippet level only
checked_by.where: https://cs.mcgill.ca/~akroit/math/analgeo/Sarnak Recent Progress on the Quantum Unique Ergodicity Conjecture.pdf

events.direction: Confirms the conjecture for the arithmetic Hecke case; cuts the way the conjecture predicts (Liouville is the only limit).

events.what_happened: Roman Holowinsky and Kannan Soundararajan, ‘Mass equidistribution for Hecke eigenforms’, arXiv 0809.1636 (first submitted 9 September 2008). Abstract: ‘We prove a conjecture of Rudnick and Sarnak on the mass equidistribution of Hecke eigenforms.’ Per the Annals listing (title ‘Quantum unique ergodicity for SL2(Z)∖H’, Annals 172 (2010)), this rules out escape of mass for Hecke eigenforms on the modular surface and completes arithmetic QUE there together with Lindenstrauss.
events.revisions: Annals of Mathematics 172 (2010) per the Annals listing (search result, not opened).
events.delivers: Mass equidistribution (QUE) for Hecke eigenforms on the modular surface SL2(Z)∖H, with no escape of mass; per secondary summaries it covers holomorphic and Maass forms. Restricted to Hecke eigenforms on the one non-compact arithmetic surface.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks beyond Hecke eigenforms on SL2(Z)∖H: compact negatively curved manifolds, non-Hecke orthonormal bases, and other quotients.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted for publication (Annals 172, 2010), per the Annals listing

events.direction: Confirms QUE for the Hecke-eigenform case on the modular surface; cuts the way the conjecture predicts.

events.what_happened: Nalini Anantharaman, ‘Entropy and the localization of eigenfunctions’, Annals of Mathematics 168 (2008) 435–475; an expository version appeared in Séminaire EDP 2006–2007. For compact negatively curved manifolds (needs only that the geodesic flow is Anosov; any dimension; variable curvature), every semiclassical measure has positive Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy, bounded below by a positive constant. Consequence: no semiclassical measure is carried by a single closed geodesic.
events.revisions: Annals 168 (2008); earlier expository version Séminaire EDP 2006–2007 (search result). arXiv posting not checked.
events.delivers: A positive lower bound on the KS entropy of every semiclassical measure of a compact negatively curved manifold, with a constant that is positive but not explicit; this rules out measures carried by finitely many closed geodesics. It does not identify any measure as Liouville.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks beyond ruling out closed-geodesic limits: identification of the only limit as Liouville, for all eigenfunction sequences.
events.direction: Partial, in the QUE direction: excludes the most obvious counter-scenario (limits on closed geodesics) but gives no identification of the limit.

events.what_happened: Nalini Anantharaman, Herbert Koch and Stéphane Nonnenmacher, ‘Entropy of eigenfunctions’, arXiv 0704.1564 (first submitted 12 April 2007). Per the abstract, it reviews an earlier lower bound on the Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy of semiclassical measures and improves it in variable negative curvature. Abstract opened; full text not read; journal status not checked.
events.delivers: An improved lower bound on the KS entropy of semiclassical measures on compact variable-negative-curvature manifolds. A secondary summary gives H_KS ≥ max(c_M, ∫log J^u dμ − (d−1)λ_max/2); this was not checked against the paper.
events.remains: Identification of the limit as Liouville: per the secondary summary the bound falls short of the Liouville entropy, so it does not force maximal entropy in general.
events.direction: Partial, same direction as anantharaman-2008-annals: a quantitative entropy bound, no identification of the limit.

events.what_happened: Semyon Dyatlov and Long Jin, ‘Semiclassical measures on hyperbolic surfaces have full support’, arXiv 1705.05019 (May 2017, month from the identifier); Acta Mathematica 220 (2018). For compact hyperbolic (constant-curvature) surfaces, every semiclassical measure has full support. Known from search-result text only; not opened.
events.delivers: Full support of every semiclassical measure on compact constant-curvature hyperbolic surfaces: no limit is carried by a proper closed invariant set, so no closed-geodesic scar. Surfaces of constant curvature only.
events.remains: Identification of the limit as Liouville (QUE); variable curvature; dimensions above two.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted for publication (Acta 220, 2018), per search result

events.direction: Partial, in the QUE direction: rules out closed-geodesic limits in constant curvature.

events.what_happened: Semyon Dyatlov, Long Jin and Stéphane Nonnenmacher, ‘Control of eigenfunctions on surfaces of variable curvature’, arXiv 1906.08923 (v1 21 June 2019; v2 16 March 2021); Journal of the AMS 35 (2022) 361–465 (published electronically 16 August 2021). For compact negatively curved surfaces of variable curvature (and more generally Anosov geodesic flows on surfaces), a microlocal lower bound on eigenfunction mass, and every semiclassical measure has full support. Also gives controllability and damped-wave decay. Known from search-result text; not opened.
events.delivers: Full support of every semiclassical measure on compact surfaces of negative variable curvature (dimension 2 only). No limit is carried by a proper closed invariant set; the identity of the limit is not given.
events.remains: QUE (identity of the limit as Liouville) for all such surfaces; all dimensions of at least 3.

checked_by.who: Referees of the Journal of the AMS
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted for publication (JAMS 35, 2022), per search result

events.direction: Partial, in the QUE direction: full support in variable negative curvature for surfaces.

events.what_happened: Andrew Hassell, ‘Ergodic billiards that are not quantum unique ergodic’ (with an appendix by Hassell and Luc Hillairet), arXiv 0807.0666 (July 2008, month from the identifier); Annals of Mathematics 171 (2010) 605–618. For a one-parameter family of partially rectangular Euclidean billiard domains (including stadium-type domains with ergodic billiard flow), the Laplacian is not QUE for aspect ratios t in [1,2], excluding a set of measure zero (per the published abstract). Known from search-result text; not opened.
events.revisions: Arxiv v3 abstract lists Dirichlet or Neumann boundary conditions; the published abstract adds Robin conditions. Annals 171 (2010).
events.delivers: Counterexamples to QUE for ergodic but non-negatively-curved billiard domains with flat rectangular parts: exceptional eigenfunction sequences localise on bouncing-ball orbits. Restricted to Euclidean billiards with boundary.
events.remains: All of problem_asks: this is a boundaried, flat setting, and the negatively curved, boundaryless case is untouched.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted for publication (Annals 171, 2010), per search result

events.direction: Cuts against QUE in general, but in a class the bullet does not cover (Euclidean billiards with boundary, not negatively curved manifolds).
events.object: A one-parameter family of partially rectangular billiard domains (the Bunimovich stadium, the Sinai billiard and Donnelly surfaces are named as examples), indexed by aspect ratio t in [1,2]. The exceptional eigenfunction sequences concentrate on bouncing-ball modes in the flat rectangular part. Established by asymptotic analysis; the abstract does not say whether the sequence is explicit.

events.what_happened: Shimon Brooks and Elon Lindenstrauss, ‘Joint quasimodes, positive entropy, and quantum unique ergodicity’, arXiv 1112.5311 (22 December 2011); Inventiones Mathematicae 2014 per a secondary search (journal reference not on the arXiv page). For compact congruence surfaces, joint quasimodes of the Laplacian and one Hecke operator, under order conditions, have positive entropy on almost every ergodic component and so satisfy QUE.
events.revisions: Inventiones 2014 per secondary search; not confirmed on the arXiv page.
events.delivers: QUE for joint quasimodes of the Laplacian and one Hecke operator on compact congruence surfaces under order conditions. The abstract also mentions an equidistribution result for compact irreducible quotients of H×H.
events.remains: General negatively curved manifolds; quasimodes not of this Hecke form; all non-arithmetic cases.
events.direction: Confirms QUE for arithmetic quasimodes; in the QUE direction.

events.what_happened: Paul D. Nelson, Ameya Pitale and Abhishek Saha, ‘Bounds for Rankin–Selberg integrals and quantum unique ergodicity for powerful levels’, arXiv 1205.5534 (May 2012, month from the identifier); Journal of the AMS 27 (2014) 147–191. For newforms of level q and weight k, the mass equidistributes as qk grows, including non-squarefree (powerful) levels, with a power saving. Known from search-result text; not opened.
events.delivers: Mass equidistribution (QUE-type) for holomorphic newforms of powerful level with a power saving, including the depth aspect. Arithmetic and holomorphic.
events.remains: Negatively curved manifolds; non-arithmetic cases; all Laplacian eigenfunction sequences.

checked_by.who: Referees of the Journal of the AMS
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted for publication (JAMS 27, 2014), per search result

events.direction: Arithmetic, holomorphic, in the QUE direction; does not touch the bullet's class.

events.what_happened: Peter Humphries, ‘Equidistribution in shrinking sets and L⁴-norm bounds for automorphic forms’, arXiv 1705.05488 (May 2017, month from the identifier); Mathematische Annalen 2018. Shows mass equidistributes in almost every shrinking hyperbolic ball of radius above the Planck scale; conditional on the generalised Lindelöf hypothesis for Hecke–Maass forms, unconditional for Eisenstein series; shows equidistribution need not hold at or below the Planck scale. Known from search-result text; not opened.
events.delivers: Averaged QUE in shrinking balls on arithmetic surfaces, above the Planck scale (Hecke–Maass conditional on GLH, Eisenstein unconditional). Not whole-surface QUE.
events.remains: All of problem_asks: whole-manifold QUE, the full sequence, and general negatively curved manifolds.
events.direction: Partial and arithmetic; in the QUE direction where it holds; notes failure below the Planck scale.

events.what_happened: Zvi Shem-Tov and Lior Silberman, ‘Arithmetic quantum unique ergodicity for products of hyperbolic 2- and 3-spaces’, arXiv 2206.05955 (first submitted 13 June 2022; last revised 26 January 2025). The introduction opens: ‘We prove the Arithmetic Quantum Unique Ergodicity Conjecture for hyperbolic 3-manifolds’; Theorem 1 covers quotients Γ∖(H²)^r × (H³)^s. Method: induction on the dimension of the orbit, ruling out limit measures on closed orbits of proper subgroups. Journal status not found.
events.revisions: v2 26 January 2025 (inside the window). No journal reference found.
events.delivers: Unconditional QUE (weak-* to the uniform measure) for joint Hecke–Maass eigenfunctions on arithmetic congruence quotients of products of H² and H³, in dimensions 2 and 3.
events.remains: Non-arithmetic hyperbolic manifolds; dimension 4 and above; general negatively curved manifolds; non-Hecke eigenbases.
events.direction: In the QUE direction, arithmetic and unconditional in its stated scope.

events.what_happened: Ankit Bisain, Peter Humphries, Andrei Mandelshtam, Noah Walsh and Xun Wang, ‘Subconvexity implies effective quantum unique ergodicity for Hecke–Maaß cusp forms on SL2(Z)∖SL2(R)’, arXiv 2402.14050 (first submitted 21 February 2024; v2 6 September 2024); Essential Number Theory 3 (2024) 101–144 (MSP; published 26 September 2024 per the MSP page). Phase-space QUE with a power-saving rate for Hecke–Maaß forms on the modular surface, conditional on three named subconvexity bounds for adjoint L-functions; under the generalised Lindelöf hypothesis the rate is λ^(−1/4+ε).
events.revisions: v2 6 September 2024. Journal: Essential Number Theory 3 (2024) pp. 101–144 (MSP page, search result).
events.delivers: Effective phase-space QUE for Hecke–Maaß cusp forms on the modular surface with a power-saving rate, but conditional on subconvexity bounds the paper says are not yet known unconditionally. The theorem makes no unconditional rate claim. Arithmetic modular surface only.
events.remains: Unconditional QUE on the modular surface (the subconvexity inputs); all general negatively curved manifolds; all general eigenbases.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted 6 September 2024 and published (per the MSP page, search result)

events.doubts: The result depends on three subconvexity bounds the paper itself says are not yet known unconditionally. This is a hypothesis of the theorem, not a doubt about its proof.
events.direction: Conditional, arithmetic, in the QUE direction: in this case the Liouville identity holds under the stated hypotheses.

events.what_happened: Zvi Shem-Tov and Lior Silberman, ‘Homogeneity of arithmetic quantum limits for hyperbolic 4-manifolds’, arXiv 2402.18218 (v1 28 February 2024; v2 3 April 2024). For normalised joint Hecke–Maass eigenfunctions on the non-compact arithmetic quotient Γ∖H⁴, every weak-* limit of the mass measures is a convex combination of the Riemannian probability measure and measures on totally geodesic 3-dimensional submanifolds. The authors describe the work as toward AQUE; escape of mass and concentration on 3-dimensional submanifolds are left open.
events.delivers: Structure of the limits: on the arithmetic non-compact quotient of H⁴, the only possible non-uniform limit mass lies on totally geodesic 3-submanifolds. Limit identification is not given. Restricted to arithmetic noncompact quotients in dimension 4.
events.remains: Full AQUE in dimension 4 (identification of the uniform limit, escape of mass, and the 3-dimensional submanifold contributions); all general negatively curved manifolds.
events.direction: Partial, in the QUE direction: restricts the non-uniform part of any limit to a specified totally geodesic family without excluding it.

events.what_happened: Alexandre de Faveri and Zvi Shem-Tov, ‘Non-escape of mass for arithmetic quantum limits on hyperbolic 4-manifolds’, arXiv 2405.04221 (v1 7 May 2024). Theorem 1: for joint Hecke–Maass eigenfunctions on the congruence quotient SV2(Z)∖H⁴, mass cannot escape; any weak-* limit is a probability measure. Theorem 2 (combined with 2402.18218): any limit is a countable convex combination of the Riemannian measure and measures on totally geodesic codimension-1 hypersurfaces. Acknowledgements give NSF DMS-1926686 and ERC HomDyn 833423.
events.revisions: v1 7 May 2024 read; later versions not checked.
events.delivers: Non-escape of mass and a limit structure for Hecke–Maass eigenfunctions on SV2(Z)∖H⁴. Full QUE is not proved. Restricted to that arithmetic quotient in dimension 4.
events.remains: Full AQUE in dimension 4 (uniform identification of the limit); all compact and general negatively curved manifolds.
events.direction: Partial, in the QUE direction: no escape of mass, and the only other limits are totally geodesic.

events.what_happened: Elena Kim and Nicholas Miller, ‘Semiclassical measures on hyperbolic manifolds’, arXiv 2503.01528 (v1 3 March 2025; v2 22 April 2025). For compact hyperbolic (n+1)-manifolds in every dimension, not restricted to arithmetic ones: the support of every semiclassical measure of Laplace eigenfunctions contains the cosphere bundle of a compact immersed totally geodesic submanifold of dimension at least 2 (Theorem 1.1). Remark: on compact hyperbolic 3-manifolds with no totally geodesic surfaces (infinitely many commensurability classes, per the authors), every semiclassical measure has full support. Method: the Dyatlov–Jin argument with Ratner theory and a generalised fractal uncertainty principle.
events.revisions: v2 22 April 2025. Dyatlov talk abstracts (Cambridge listing, 2025 and January 2026) describe the work; these are listings, not verifications.
events.delivers: A constraint on the support of any semiclassical measure on compact hyperbolic manifolds of any dimension: its support contains a totally geodesic cosphere bundle, or it has full support. This does not identify the measure and does not show Liouville is the only one. It is the one in-window result on compact non-arithmetic manifolds.
events.remains: Whether a non-Liouville limit exists; QUE for all compact negatively curved manifolds; the variable-curvature case. Full support does not by itself imply Liouville.
events.direction: Restricts the possible non-Liouville limits on compact hyperbolic manifolds to measures whose support contains a totally geodesic cosphere bundle, or else has full support. It neither contradicts nor confirms QUE.

events.what_happened: Paul D. Nelson, ‘Subconvexity implies quantum unique ergodicity for GL(2)’, arXiv 2505.13256 (v1 19 May 2025); v2 retitled ‘Soft bounds for local triple products and the subconvexity-QUE implication for GL2’. Unconditional soft bounds for local and global triple-product integrals (Theorems 1 and 6). Theorem 8: QUE follows from a subconvexity-type condition on triple-product L-values (conditional). Theorem 11: effective phase-space QUE, also conditional.
events.revisions: v2 retitled; v2 date not checked.
events.delivers: The unconditional triple-product bounds, and the implication from subconvexity to QUE (and effective QUE) for GL2 automorphic forms. The paper proves no unconditional QUE.
events.remains: Unconditional QUE for GL2; general negatively curved manifolds; all other eigenfunction classes.
events.direction: Conditional, arithmetic (GL2), in the QUE direction; reduces QUE to subconvexity.

events.what_happened: Qingfeng Sun and Qizhi Zhang, ‘Equidistribution of holomorphic cusp forms on thin sets’, arXiv 2511.12465 (v1 16 November 2025; later v2). Averaged over an orthonormal basis of weight-k cusp forms for SL2(Z), the weighted restriction integrals over thin sets R in H converge to (3/π) times the integral against a natural measure on R. Corollaries cover the vertical geodesic, a horizontal segment and the modular surface.
events.revisions: v2 (later); the abstracts of v1 and v2 differ in wording.
events.delivers: Averaged restricted QUE for holomorphic Hecke cusp forms on the modular surface, on thin sets; averaged over the basis, not for individual forms.
events.remains: Individual-form restricted QUE (Young’s rQUE); all of problem_asks (Laplacian eigenfunctions on negatively curved manifolds).
events.direction: In the restricted-QUE direction, but for averaged holomorphic arithmetic objects; not the bullet's claim.

events.what_happened: Doyon Kim and Youngmin Lee, ‘Quantum ergodicity of Eisenstein series for Bianchi groups’, arXiv 2603.16518 (17 March 2026), math.NT. For each cusp of PSL2(O_F)∖H³ (F imaginary quadratic with class number greater than 1), the ratio μ_{η,t}(A)/μ_{η,t}(B) of |E_η(·,1+it)|² dV tends to Vol(A)/Vol(B) as t → ∞. Ratio-form quantum ergodicity for Eisenstein series, not density-one and not QUE with respect to a normalised measure.
events.delivers: Ratio-form quantum ergodicity for Eisenstein series on a non-compact arithmetic Bianchi 3-orbifold, unconditional per the statement.
events.remains: All of problem_asks: this is an Eisenstein series, non-compact, arithmetic, and a ratio statement.
events.direction: Consistent with equidistribution, but not a QUE statement for the bullet's class.

events.what_happened: Maximiliano Sanchez Garza, ‘Equidistribution in shrinking sets for arithmetic spherical harmonics’, arXiv 2603.00790 (v1 28 February 2026; revised 25 March 2026), math.NT. Under the generalised Lindelöf hypothesis, mass equidistributes on shrinking spherical caps of radius considerably above the Planck scale; explicit Wasserstein and cap-discrepancy bounds.
events.delivers: Conditional QUE in shrinking caps for arithmetic spherical harmonics on the round sphere (positive curvature).
events.remains: All of problem_asks: the setting is not negatively curved and the statement is not for the full sequence.
events.direction: Positive-curvature analogue; not a result about the bullet's class.

events.what_happened: Alexandre de Faveri and Zvi Shem-Tov, ‘Mass equidistribution for lifts on hyperbolic 4-manifolds’, arXiv 2603.01817 (v1 2 March 2026; v2 5 March 2026; v3 6 September 2026). Theorem 1 (‘QUE for Pitale lifts’): for the Pitale lifts ψ_n (non-holomorphic Saito–Kurokawa analogues lifted from weight-1/2 Kohnen-plus Hecke–Maass forms), normalised in L², the measures |ψ_n|² dz converge weak-* to the uniform probability measure on the non-uniform arithmetic quotient SV2(Z)∖H⁴, along the whole sequence. Main new ingredient: an amplifier ruling out concentration along non-tempered homogeneous submanifolds. The authors say the general Hecke–Maass case is ongoing joint work with Simon Marshall. Funding: NSF DMS-1926686, ERC HomDyn 833423.
events.revisions: v2 5 March 2026; v3 6 September 2026 (what changed in v3 not identified).
events.delivers: Unconditional, full-sequence QUE for one explicit family (the Pitale lifts) of Hecke–Maass forms on the non-uniform arithmetic quotient SV2(Z)∖H⁴. Restricted to that family and that quotient.
events.remains: QUE for all Hecke–Maass forms on SV2(Z)∖H⁴ and on other quotients (ongoing per the authors); all compact negatively curved manifolds; general eigenbases.
events.direction: In the QUE direction, unconditional, for one family in an arithmetic non-compact dimension-4 setting.

events.what_happened: Elena Kim, ‘Characterizing the support of semiclassical measures for higher-dimensional cat maps’, arXiv 2410.13449 (October 2024, month from the identifier). For quantised higher-dimensional cat maps (a toral system, not a negatively curved manifold): when the characteristic polynomial of every power of the cat matrix is irreducible over Q, every semiclassical measure has full support, via Cohen’s higher-dimensional fractal uncertainty principle. The abstract says cat maps allow counterexamples to QUE. A Princeton seminar listing attributes a higher-dimensional QUE counterexample for cat maps to Kim; no separate arXiv listing for it was located. Abstract known from search text; not opened.
events.delivers: Full support of semiclassical measures for quantised higher-dimensional cat maps under an irreducibility hypothesis. Not a manifold statement.
events.remains: Not applicable to the bullet's class; the cat-map system is only an analogue.
events.direction: Cat-map counterexamples to QUE-type equidistribution exist in that class; cat maps are not negatively curved manifolds, so this cuts only by analogy.
events.object: Higher-dimensional quantised cat maps (toral). The seminar-listed counterexample is said to extend Faure–Nonnenmacher–De Bièvre’s construction; not verified.

events.what_happened: Kurlberg, Ostafe, Rudnick and Shparlinski, ‘On quantum ergodicity for higher dimensional cat maps’, arXiv 2411.05997 (November 2024, month from the identifier). Under stated assumptions, a density-one sequence of integers N along which all eigenfunctions of the quantised higher-dimensional cat map are uniformly distributed. Abstract known from search text; not opened.
events.delivers: Density-one quantum ergodicity for quantised higher-dimensional cat maps under assumptions. Not QUE, and not a manifold statement.
events.remains: Full-sequence QUE; the bullet's class entirely.
events.direction: Positive density-one statement for a different system; neighbouring, not on the bullet.

summary: Searched to 13 October 2026. The conjecture as worded (every negatively curved manifold, every eigenfunction sequence, convergence to Liouville) is still open in every source read: no preprint, journal article or lab announcement claims it, and the 2024–2026 sources describe it as a conjecture (Nonnenmacher’s June 2026 survey, arXiv 2606.12098; Kim–Miller’s introduction). Since 26 January 2024 the restricted cases moved. Arithmetic: Shem-Tov–Silberman’s dimension-4 limit structure (Feb 2024); de Faveri–Shem-Tov’s non-escape of mass in dimension 4 (May 2024); Bisain et al.’s effective QUE for the modular surface, conditional on subconvexity (Feb 2024); Nelson’s subconvexity-to-QUE implication for GL2 (May 2025, conditional); Sun–Zhang’s averaged restricted QUE for holomorphic forms (Nov 2025); and de Faveri–Shem-Tov’s unconditional full-sequence QUE for the Pitale lifts on the non-uniform quotient SV2(Z)∖H⁴ (March 2026). Non-arithmetic: Kim–Miller (March 2025) shows that the support of every semiclassical measure on a compact hyperbolic manifold of any dimension contains a totally geodesic cosphere bundle, or else is of full support. That is a constraint, not an identification of the limit. Close call 1: the Pitale-lift theorem is a true full-sequence QUE, but for one family on a non-compact arithmetic quotient, so it does not settle the bullet. Close call 2: whether Kim–Miller counts as progress on the general case. Full support does not give Liouville, so I read it as structural only, and the competing reading is in competing_reading. Scope note: the bullet does not say compact; the literature version does, and the record keeps the bullet’s wording. Nothing in the window is a retraction or a dispute. Human checking: none found beyond journal acceptance for the older papers; the 2024–2026 preprints have only seminar listings and no written verification. AI: no source read credits a system with any of the mathematics. Full-text checks of the in-window arithmetic papers found no AI mention, and their acknowledgements list grants only. OpenAI’s openai/math repository (719 manuscripts in 372 families, per its README) has no entry on QUE, semiclassical measures or Liouville; I read the full family index (001–377) through summarising fetches, not the manuscripts. OpenAI’s August 2026 Astra results (ten problems, per news coverage) and DeepMind’s Aletheia work (Erdős problems, FirstProof, eigenweights) include nothing on this bullet. No Lean or mathlib formalisation of QUE was found. Neighbouring AI-spectral items, not on this bullet: a Henkel talk on an AI-assisted Hodge-Laplacian eigenvalue proof (self-reported in a talk abstract); arXiv 2608.01673 (Codex, lattice eigenfunctions, AI-use declaration seen in a search snippet only); arXiv 2606.23821 (AI-assisted numerical verification). The Wikipedia ‘Quantum ergodicity’ article (edited 16 August 2026) does not mention the conjecture; the list bullet (footnote 38) was not followed to its source.
competing_reading: Read de Faveri–Shem-Tov’s March 2026 Pitale-lift theorem as the strongest in-window QUE result, and count the problem as moved within a sub-case. The bullet’s universal statement is untouched, so this does not change its general status. Read Kim–Miller (March 2025) as partial progress on the non-arithmetic compact case, because it excludes some non-Liouville limits. The conjecture requires Liouville to be the unique limit, and full support does not give that. A reader who counts any scar-type obstruction as relevant would also weigh Kim–Miller’s totally geodesic obstruction as a warning that QUE may fail in some compact hyperbolic manifolds, which the record does not claim.
what_would_settle_it: For the general status: a published, checked proof (or a verified counterexample) identifying all semiclassical measures on a compact negatively curved manifold that is not arithmetic, or the completion of the authors’ general Hecke–Maass programme (ongoing per de Faveri–Shem-Tov). For the in-window items: journal status and any later citations of the 2024–2026 preprints, which this search could not establish. For the AI question: a statement by the authors of any of these papers naming a model; none exists in the sources read.

event.what_happened: Alexandre de Faveri and Zvi Shem-Tov, ‘Mass equidistribution for lifts on hyperbolic 4-manifolds’, arXiv 2603.01817 (v1 2 March 2026; v2 5 March 2026; v3 6 September 2026). Theorem 1 (‘QUE for Pitale lifts’): for the Pitale lifts ψ_n (non-holomorphic Saito–Kurokawa analogues lifted from weight-1/2 Kohnen-plus Hecke–Maass forms), normalised in L², the measures |ψ_n|² dz converge weak-* to the uniform probability measure on the non-uniform arithmetic quotient SV2(Z)∖H⁴, along the whole sequence. Main new ingredient: an amplifier ruling out concentration along non-tempered homogeneous submanifolds. The authors say the general Hecke–Maass case is ongoing joint work with Simon Marshall. Funding: NSF DMS-1926686, ERC HomDyn 833423.
event.revisions: v2 5 March 2026; v3 6 September 2026 (what changed in v3 not identified).
event.delivers: Unconditional, full-sequence QUE for one explicit family (the Pitale lifts) of Hecke–Maass forms on the non-uniform arithmetic quotient SV2(Z)∖H⁴. Restricted to that family and that quotient.
event.remains: QUE for all Hecke–Maass forms on SV2(Z)∖H⁴ and on other quotients (ongoing per the authors); all compact negatively curved manifolds; general eigenbases.
event.direction: In the QUE direction, unconditional, for one family in an arithmetic non-compact dimension-4 setting.

judgement.why: The statement is the full QUE conjecture for negatively curved manifolds. Unconditional proofs that Liouville is the only limit for a restricted class of eigenfunctions on a restricted class of (arithmetic, negatively curved, finite-volume) manifolds count as `case`: Lindenstrauss, Holowinsky–Soundararajan, Brooks–Lindenstrauss, Shem-Tov–Silberman 2022 (its 2025 v2 shows no new mathematics, so it stays a 2022 event) and the March 2026 Pitale-lift theorem, which is the only post-snapshot case and is an unreviewed preprint. The entropy lower bounds are `bound`s on a quantity. Full-support, limit-structure and non-escape results (Dyatlov–Jin, Dyatlov–Jin–Nonnenmacher, Kim–Miller, Shem-Tov–Silberman H⁴, de Faveri–Shem-Tov 2024) constrain the limits without identifying them, so they are `none`: steps toward a proof, not a settled restriction. Conditional results (Bisain et al., Nelson 2025) reduce QUE to unproven subconvexity, so they are `none`. Different objects or settings are `variant`: billiards, holomorphic forms, shrinking sets, averaged thin sets, Eisenstein series, spheres and cat maps. No event credits any AI system.
judgement.doubts: Treating arithmetic Hecke QUE as a `case` rather than a `variant` is a judgement call, because the conjecture concerns every eigenbasis. It is kept as `case` because the Hecke eigenfunctions are genuine Laplacian eigenfunctions on negatively curved manifolds, and the literature calls this the proven case. The Pitale-lift paper has no reviewer engagement, and the record does not say what changed in its v3. The Brooks–Lindenstrauss journal status rests on a secondary source only.
